title: Finite-ring and uniform-tower domains of a smooth tensor transpose
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. All schemes in this statement are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the ordinary uncompleted constant-coefficient pro-etale module derived categories and their bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Pullbacks and tensor products are the ordinary derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-tensor].
Let $v:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary. For a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$, write $\mathcal C_T(A)$ for the bounded intrinsically constructible finite-Tor subcategory of the ordinary derived category. Every $K\in\mathcal C_Y(A)$ admits a bounded representative with flat constructible terms. If $K\in\mathcal C_Y(A)$ and $P$ is any such bounded representative with flat constructible terms, zero outside $[a,b]$ with $a\le b$, then $v^*P$ has flat constructible terms, is K-flat and represents $v^*K$. It is zero outside $[a,b]$. The object $v^*K$ belongs to $\mathcal C_{Y'}(A)$, and tensoring it with any module sheaf in degree zero has cohomology only in $[a,b]$. For every $i$, $\mathcal H^i(v^*K)=v^*\mathcal H^i(K)$. Every finite constructible stratification for $P^i$ or $\mathcal H^i(K)$ pulls back to one for its inverse image, with the same finite local module models on the pulled-back trivializing covers.

For $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. Use the ordinary varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Let $K_\bullet$ have constructible levels with common cohomological bounds $[c,e]$ and common Tor bounds $[a,b]$, in the sense of [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], without a normalization assumption. Exact levelwise pullback $v_\bullet^*K_\bullet$ has the same cohomological and Tor bounds and constructible levels. When the ramification index is $r$, the level $n$ assertion uses $A_n=A_{E,rn}$.

In either coefficient setting, form a Cartesian square $fu=vf'$ with $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$, $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ [def-pc-base-change, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $B$ denote $A$ or $A_\bullet$, let $\omega_{f,B}=f_B^!B_Y$, $\omega_{f',B}=f_B'^!B_{Y'}$, with their oriented tensor constructions [det-sp-finite-general-ring, det-sp-tower-gamma], and suppose $e_1:u_B^*\omega_{f,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f',B}$. Then $f_B'^*v_B^*K\otimes^L\omega_{f',B}$ and $u_B^*(f_B^*K\otimes^L\omega_{f,B})$ belong to the indicated constructible finite-Tor category and are canonically isomorphic by the monoidal comparison followed by $1\otimes e_1$. Thus they are inputs to the restricted adjunction $F_{f',B}\dashv G_{f',B}$ [def-pur-co-smoothness, det-sp-tower-gluing].

proof.text: Pull back the stratification and the actual finite local module models, as in the existing stratification_local_models proof. The finite-model criteria identify this constructibility predicate with the fixed-module source predicate, including empty schemes.

Use intrinsicOrigin to descend the finite bounded constructible finite-Tor complex to the etale site. Reflect the chosen Tor interval and apply the bounded flat constructible model theorem there. Exact comparison sends this model to the requested pro-etale representative. For an arbitrary supplied bounded flat constructible representative, exact inverse image preserves flatness, constructibility and zero terms. The bounded flat criterion proves K-flatness and the Tor interval. mapDerivedCategoryFactors and the exact homology comparison give the representative and every cohomology isomorphism.

For the finite tensor source apply the existing proObjectsCtf theorem to the dualizing complex. The finite comparison-adjunction unit is invertible on the degree-zero coefficient unit; its exceptional image identifies the comparison of the dualizing complex with finiteOmega. Pull back this source along u. Transport constructible finite-Tor membership through finiteComparison to obtain the other source. Thus no independent smoothness calculation for f-prime is needed.

For towers use levelComparison, the realization counit and pullEvaluation to identify every actual pullback level with constant-ring inverse image. Apply finite_constant_pullback_bounds, which allows arbitrary finite rings, at the actual ell-power quotient and the given Tor endpoints. Exact inverse image and its homology comparison preserve the given cohomological endpoints as well. No normalization and no residue-level replacement is needed.

The existing unit_tower_mem theorem supplies the actual coefficient unit. The given G already lands in the full uniform constructible finite-Tor category, so G of that unit belongs to it. Pullback preserves the domain by the preceding step. Apply ordinary uniform tensor closure to the pullback of K and G of the unit, then use the realization counit to identify the resulting system tensor with the actual displayed source.

Pull back the source for f along u, preserving uniform constructible finite-Tor membership. The actual towerComparison is the monoidal pullback comparison followed by the square comparison and tensor with e1. Transport membership through its inverse-realization image. This proves both tower domains without replacing the actual system comparison by levelwise maps.
